prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When an OAuthClientProvider is re-instantiated (e.g., after a process restart) and loads a previously-stored token, `OAuthContext.token_expiry_time` is never repopulated from `current_tokens.expires_in`. prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Naive comma-splitting when parsing the WWW-Authenticate header's auth-params lets commas inside quoted values (or a second challenge/scheme present in the same header) incorrectly terminate or bleed into a parameter, causing wrong values to be extracted in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py. prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs add the same quote/escape-aware comma splitter at the same spot in utils.py, but #3041 goes further: it splits the whole header into segments and then specifically locates the 'Bearer' scheme's segment (_extract_bearer_auth_params), so it correctly handles a WWW-Authenticate header containing multiple challenges (e.g. Digest and Bearer combined via commas, as allowed by RFC 7235). #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips the text before the first space and treats everything after it as one flat parameter list, which assumes a single scheme is present and would misparse a header containing more than one challenge.

Both PRs add a helper to detect 'string-compatible' annotations and skip pre-parsing for them. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2032's _should_pre_parse_json checks get_args() membership against a raw _SIMPLE_TYPES set (str/int/float/bool/NoneType) without unwrapping nested Annotated, so the common FastMCP idiom `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` still fails the check (the arg is an Annotated object, not literally `str`) and remains buggy - it only fixes the outer-Annotated form `Annotated[str | None, Field(...)]`. #3056 adds an explicit _unwrap_annotated step before comparison, so `Optional[Annotated[str, Field(...)]]` is correctly detected and skipped. #3056 also scopes the fix to str|None specifically (with an explanatory docstring on why broader unions like str|int aren't safe to skip), whereas #2032's broader _SIMPLE_TYPES set silently changes pre-parsing behavior for str|int/str|float/str|bool unions beyond what the reported bug covers.

prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a restart, `OAuthContext.oauth_metadata` (the discovered authorization server metadata, including the token endpoint) is only held in memory and is lost, so a cold-start token refresh has no way to resolve the correct token endpoint without redoing full discovery. prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2492 fixes this by adding optional `get_oauth_metadata`/`set_oauth_metadata` hooks to the `TokenStorage` protocol that default to no-ops, so unless a given storage backend explicitly implements persistence, restart behavior is unchanged and the bug persists for most existing implementations. #3263 instead makes `_refresh_token` perform AS metadata discovery itself before a cold-start refresh (tracked via the new `eager_discovery_attempted` flag, reusing the eager-discovery machinery so a metadata-less server isn't re-probed on every refresh), which fixes the problem universally regardless of the storage backend in use, and additionally adds an issuer-binding check on the rediscovered metadata that #2492 does not have.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs add the same quote/escape-aware comma splitter at the same spot in utils.py, but #3041 goes further: it splits the whole header into segments and then specifically locates the 'Bearer' scheme's segment (_extract_bearer_auth_params), so it correctly handles a WWW-Authenticate header containing multiple challenges (e.g. Digest and Bearer combined via commas, as allowed by RFC 7235). #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips the text before the first space and treats everything after it as one flat parameter list, which assumes a single scheme is present and would misparse a header containing more than one challenge.
